definitions.explanation: A diplomatic representative of a country, ranking below an ambassador. Historically the chief representative sent to countries with which full ambassadorial relations had not been established.

examples.japanese: {公使|こうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{会談|かいだん}→会談：11542_kaidan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出席|しゅっせき}した→出席する：01830_shussekisuru⟧。
{特命|とくめい}{全権|ぜんけん}{公使|こうし}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{派遣|はけん}→派遣：13273_haken⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He was dispatched as minister plenipotentiary.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}→明治時代：28080_meijijidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{公使|こうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{派遣|はけん}→派遣：13273_haken⟧⟦され→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{外交|がいこう}→外交：02627_gaikou⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{築|きず}かれた→築く：02046_kizuku⟧。
examples.english: During the Meiji era, ministers were dispatched to many countries and diplomatic relations were established.

notes:
Composed of {公|こう} (public, official) and {使|し} (envoy, messenger).

In modern diplomacy, most countries exchange ambassadors (⟦{大使|たいし}→大使：03391_taishi⟧) rather than ministers. The rank of {公使|こうし} is now less common but still exists in some diplomatic contexts and appears frequently in historical texts about the Meiji and Taisho periods.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {特命|とくめい}{全権|ぜんけん}{公使|こうし} (minister plenipotentiary)
- {公使|こうし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{派遣|はけん}→派遣：13273_haken⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to dispatch a minister)
- {公使|こうし}{館|かん} (legation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {公使|こうし}: minister (lower diplomatic rank)
- ⟦{大使|たいし}→大使：03391_taishi⟧: ambassador (highest diplomatic rank)
- ⟦{領事|りょうじ}→領事：15209_ryouji⟧: consul (handles commercial and citizen affairs)
